item.title: Developer pitches nearly 45 affordable apartments in Humboldt Park
item.description: <p>A developer who has completed more than a dozen housing projects in Humboldt Park is proposing another development in the West Side neighborhood.</p><p>Hispanic Housing Development Corp. is seeking a zoning change to build 44 affordable apartments at 3251 W. Division St., west of the neighborhood’s namesake park. item.title: Matisse exhibition at AIC shows a creative hitting his stride in his 70s
item.description: <p>Artists follow varied career paths. Some maintain strong, steady production throughout their lifetimes. Some fade over time. Some are one-hit wonders who score success with one body of work that they can never replicate.</p><p>But few accomplish what Henri Matisse did at the end of his career when his output seemingly declined. item.title: Libertyville troubadour Ike Reilly is more vocal than ever
item.description: <p>Ike Reilly has made a career of speaking truth to power. item.title: Chicago band Brigitte Calls Me Baby is back with sophomore album ‘Irreversible’
item.description: <p>When Brigitte Bardot died last year, it’s almost like Wes Leavins knew it was coming. item.title: Dear Abby: Night spent in separate beds was a revelation
item.description: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I have been married 44 years and have always slept in the same bed with my wife. Last week, I caught a virus, and we decided that I would sleep in the spare bedroom until it was gone. I have now discovered I sleep better by myself, and I enjoy the freedom of the bed. How do I tell my wife I'd prefer sleeping alone? item.description: <p>High school students made voting history in suburban Cook County, and they did it in a single day.</p><p>Through the clerk’s new "Defenders of DA'mocracy" High School Early Voting Program, student-run early voting sites inside 24 suburban high schools recorded 1,136 ballots cast on Feb. 26. item.title: Man stabbed on Red Line platform in River North
item.description: <p>A 37-year-old man was stabbed with a sharp object while at a Red Line subway station in River North late Thursday.</p><p>The victim was standing on the platform, 521 N. State St., when an man he doesn't know approached, displayed a sharp object and attacked him shortly before midnight, police said. </p><p>The man, who suffered a puncture wound to the left tricep, was taken in fair condition to Northwestern Memorial Hospital, police said. </p><p>It wasn't clear if the attacker was arrested.
